messages.subject: Multi night/ cover type survey
parts:
Hello,
I am a student working on estimating the deer population of a large state park. I completed a 5 night road based distance sampling survey using spotlights and laser rangefinders on 32 transects. I used only dirt roads with low traffic and without roadside grazing areas for safety reasons and to potentially reduce road bias. To help alleviate the bias of using roads, I took cover type data for the sightings. I plan to find the density of deer in each cover type using distance sampling and extrapolate to the entire park.

I had a few questions about putting the data into DISTANCE.
  1. Since my survey was 5 nights long should I do analysis for each night and average the results or combine all of the sighting data?
  2. Also, in the results, why do the graphs show probability vs. sighting distance. From the YouTube videos, I thought that the graphs for this process were supposed to show the number of deer sightings vs distance and probability was calculated from this graph. and used in the equation N=(n/P)/(a/A)
  3. My transects run through multiple cover types. This has complicated analysis  since I am somewhat confused on how to enter this into DISTANCE. Currently I have each cover type entered as a region and my area is the total area of that  cover type in the park as determined with ArcGIS. Should I enter all of the transects for each cover region category? Currently, I have estimated the percent cover type for each transect and I have multiplied this by each transect length. This makes it so that the transect lengths in each cover region are the percent of the transect that matched the cover type. Does that seem reasonable?
  4. I noticed that changes in transect length do not affect the probability graph. Would it be easier for me to use the "p" value from the results and calculate N=(n/P)/(a/A) by hand for each cover region since the cover type data complicates Distance data entry?
Thank you,
-Jesse Morrison

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Multi night/ cover type survey
parts:
Jesse

Good work on your part to have numerous transects and to be conscious of the challenges of conducting surveys from roads.  I'm not clear how your recording of habitat types for each detection will resolve the sampling from roads as it is unlikely that placement of roads will necessarily equitably sample the habitat types throughout the park, but that is another issue.

To your specific questions:

1 -  combine data from all five surveys into a single project.  You are unlikely to have much precision from analysing data from each night individually.

2 - not sure how to answer this.  The software fits a detection function to the perpendicular distances, then plots the fitted function superimposed upon the histogram of perpendicular distances.

3 - from your description of your design, I gather that you did not design your survey to explicitly lay transects into particular habitat types.  Consequently, the amount of survey effort in your habitat types will arise as a result of luck rather than as a result of design.  Perhaps you will have lots of detections in each of your habitats, but chances are that some of your habitats will have little effort (consequently few detections), making the assessment of detectability and encounter rate in those habitats challenging.  Nevertheless, the answer to your question is to create a field in the observation layer for habitat, because habitat type is associated with the detections, not with the transects, then conduct post-stratification.  Your GIS work of breaking a transect into bits will actually make it appear as if you have many more than the 32 transects you actually have, creating problems for estimating variability in encounter rates between transects.

4 - true, transect lengths are needed to estimate encounter rates, but transect lengths do not influence the detectability process governing the probability of detecting animals at various perpendicular distances from the transect.

If you want to discuss your issue #3 in more detail, we could have further correspondence off the list.
